title: SLO change governance and stakeholder signoff for model rollouts
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose: Define the governance, telemetry gates, capacity checks and stakeholder signoff process for changing SLOs or SLO-related configuration during multi-stage model rollouts (hosted, dedicated, and private). This playbook ensures changes are safe for customers, preserved for regulatory evidence, and reversible with clear operational handoffs.

Scope: Applies to: model architecture swaps, quantization profile changes, tokenizer changes that affect latency/cost, SLO adjustment (target or window), error budget reallocation, and rollout routing/policy changes. Not in scope: purely offline eval metric changes unless they drive an SLO change.

Owners and roles

- Service owner: product/feature team that owns the model tenant. Responsible for the rollout proposal and customer communication.
- SLO steward: eng-sre team member responsible for SLO definitions, dashboards and verification.
- Capacity steward: infra/capacity planning lead responsible for provisioning and headroom calculations.
- Incident owner: oncall for the model-serving runtime during rollout.
- Compliance reviewer (optional): security/legal for privacy or regulated-customer impacts.

Summary of governance stages

1) Proposal (Draft)
- Trigger: PR or RFC that contains a proposed SLO or SLO-config change tied to a model rollout.
- Required artifacts: rollout PR, canary plan, telemetry and alert diff, runbook draft, headroom calculation snapshot, customer impact assessment.
- Minimum signoffs: Service owner, SLO steward.

2) Preflight (Validation)
- Actions: functional tests, offline evals vs baseline prompt-sets, telemetry shadowing, synthetic canaries in staging.
- Telemetry checks: latency Q95/Q99 baseline delta, token-cost delta, quality regressions (F1/ROUGE/LLR reduction), and new error-class rates.
- Acceptance criteria: all checks green OR documented mitigations.
- Minimum signoffs: SLO steward, Capacity steward.

3) Canary (Limited Production)
- Actions: traffic ramp to canary cohort, live telemetry sampling, automated abort rules active.
- Observability: dedicated canary dashboard with comparison panels to baseline.
- Abort window: first 60 minutes for latency and errors, full canary window 72 hours for quality and cost drift.
- Minimum signoffs to progress: Incident owner acknowledges watch schedule; SLO steward approves continuation.

4) Gradual Ramp / Staged Rollout
- Actions: traffic ramp per schedule, capacity adjustments, customer comms as needed.
- Gates: error budget consumption thresholds, headroom utilization thresholds, and sustained tail-latency increases.
- Final signoff: Service owner + SLO steward + Capacity steward.

5) Post-rollout (Evidence & Retrospective)
- Actions: capture evidence bundle, update SLO docs, schedule 2-week retrospective if change impacted SLO.
- Evidence retained: dashboards, alert firing logs, synthetic canary artifacts, blob of sampled requests (privacy redacted).

Telemetry & gating specifics

Key signals (minimum):
- Latency: P50, P95, P99 (absolute ms and % delta vs baseline).
- Error rate: grouped by failure class (OOM, ModelTimeout, DecodeError, 5xx).
- Quality: evaluation set pass-rate and production approximation signals (nps/QA sampling).
- Cost: tokens-per-request, per-token latency cost, estimated $/MM tokens per model variant.
- Headroom: available GPU slots, warm-pool counts, model memory pressure (GB free).

Automated abort rules (examples):
1) If 5xx rate for rollout cohort > 3x baseline and absolute > 0.5% for 10m -> abort.
2) If P99 latency increases by > 40% and absolute > 250ms for 5m -> throttle ramp back to previous step.
3) If error budget for tenant is consumed > 30% of monthly budget within 24h of rollout -> pause ramp and notify SLO steward.
4) If synthetic-quality regression (eval pass-rate drop) > 5% -> immediate pause.

Headroom calculation (reference formula)

- Baseline QPS = 95th percentile observed QPS over last 7 days.
- Nominal concurrency multiplier = 1.5 for burst allowance.
- Required capacity = Baseline QPS * nominal concurrency multiplier * p95_latency_seconds / tokens_per_request_factor
- Safety headroom target = max(ReservedCapacity * 0.20, Required capacity * 0.15)

Example table: capacity inputs and thresholds

| Field | Value (example) | Unit | Owner | Threshold to block rollout |
|-------|-----------------|------|-------|----------------------------|
| Baseline QPS | 120 | req/s | Service owner | - |
| P95 latency (baseline) | 0.18 | s | SLO steward | If new P95 > 0.25 s -> block |
| Reserved GPUs | 6 | GPUs | Capacity steward | If available GPUs < 2 -> block |
| Token cost delta | +12% | % | Finance owner | If > 25% -> require finance signoff |

Signoff matrix (minimum)

- Draft: Service owner, SLO steward (required)
- Preflight: SLO steward, Capacity steward (required)
- Canary: Incident owner (ack), SLO steward (required)
- Production ramp: Service owner, SLO steward, Capacity steward (all required)
- Post-rollout evidence marked: Service owner (required)

Runbook excerpts and operational tooling

1) Create canary cohort and route traffic (CLI snippet):

- rctl rollout start --service my-model --variant v2 --cohort canary-5pct --duration 72h
- rctl watch --dashboard canary-my-model-v2

2) Collect evidence bundle (single command creates archive for compliance):

- rctl evidence capture --service my-model --window 2026-02-20T00:00Z/2026-02-22T00:00Z --include=snapshots,alerts,request-samples --redact=pii --output s3://redwood-evidence/rollouts/my-model-v2-20260222.tar.gz

3) Telemetry mapping table (alert -> action):

| Alert name | Trigger | First responder | Immediate action |
|------------|---------|-----------------|------------------|
| model-rollout-latency-spike | P99 delta > 40% for 5m | oncall runtime team | Pause ramp, scale model warm pool, notify SLO steward |
| model-rollout-5xx-surge | 5xx > 3x baseline for 10m | oncall runtime team | Abort rollout, rollback routing to previous variant |
| model-rollout-quality-drop | eval pass-rate drop > 5% | product ML lead | Pause, run additional prompt-set checks |

Escalation and communication guideline

- Within first 60 minutes of canary: real-time Slack channel #rollout-watch must be monitored by incident owner and service owner.
- For any abort rule firing: incident owner runs immediate rollback command and files an incident stub (template below).
- Customer communication: product team drafts customer bulletin within 4 hours if customer-facing impact detected.

Incident stub template (fill on abort)

1) Title: [Abort] {service} {variant} {timestamp}
2) Summary: one-sentence description
3) What changed: PR/RFC link + brief description
4) Immediate impact metrics: P95/P99, 5xx delta, headroom at abort time
5) Mitigation steps taken: rollout paused/rolled back, scaling actions
6) Next steps / RCA owner: assign SLO steward and service owner

Evidence retention and audit trail

- Retain evidence for 180 days for internal compliance (longer for regulated customers; coordinate with legal).
- Evidence bundle MUST include: dashboard snapshots, alert logs, runbook invocation logs, sampled requests with PII redaction.
- Naming convention: {service}-{variant}-{startISO}-{endISO}-evidence.tar.gz

Postmortem & continuous improvement

- If rollout caused an SLO burn > 10% of monthly budget or customer-visible outage, schedule a 2-week retro and add a reliability initiative ticket.
- Maintain a short living list of durable mitigations (e.g., model warm pools, pre-quantization verification harness) and track implementation in the reliability backlog.

Appendix: checklist (quick yes/no)

- [ ] Draft RFC with SLO impact analysis uploaded
- [ ] Headroom calculation attached and verified
- [ ] Canary plan with automated abort rules documented
- [ ] Runbook snippets ready and validated in staging
- [ ] SLO steward + Capacity steward approvals captured
- [ ] Evidence capture automation enabled for canary window

Notes and references

- See related: runtime-architecture (for memory/WARM pool guidance), service-onboarding-runway (for SLO admission steps).
- Template commands use 'rctl' which wraps internal rollout APIs; replace with local tooling as appropriate.
- This document is intended to be referenced by service owners for all model variant rollouts that change SLO-relevant parameters.
